title: horizon --hook advises git merge --ff-only on a branch that is both ahead of and behind origin/main, where the fast-forward refuses
goal: lag_line names the lag with an instruction that works for the checkout's state: a branch ahead of and behind origin/main gets no --ff-only advice (a rebase or merge question instead), a branch only behind keeps the fast-forward line

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_view
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", d, "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com", *a], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
g("init", "-q"); g("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "c0"); base = g("rev-parse", "HEAD")
g("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "c1"); g("update-ref", "refs/remotes/origin/main", "HEAD")
g("reset", "-q", "--hard", base); g("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "c2")
line = bl_view.lag_line(d)
print(repr(line))
sys.exit(1 if "--ff-only" in line else 0)
